original_poem:
तुरेल नुपा यम्लैक्ख्रिबा,  
साना चंगु मगनुंगली,  
नोनी नारानबाशिगी,  
युंबिनु मग्नुम ओक्ते।

लामंग थावंग थमाइब,  
निंगोल सिंगनबाउबा,  
इयेंगुं तुंबाई ओइ,  
ताम्बा मोयोम इमो ओई।
translated_poem:
The river, a man restless and bold,  
Carving the earth with stories untold,  
Dancing with the grace of the night,  
Weaving through villages, out of sight.

The hills bow as he roars ahead,  
Carrying dreams in his riverbed,  
Whispers of love from mountain’s breast,  
The river flows on, never to rest.

stanzas.loss_note: नुपा यम्लैक्ख्रिबा (restless/bold man) carries a specific Meitei masculine vitality connotation flattened by 'restless and bold'.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: river as an untamed man driven by irrepressible inner force
golden carving as the river's purposeful shaping of the land

translated_lines: The hills bow as he roars ahead,

stanzas.loss_note: निंगोल सिंगनबाउबा (a woman longing/yearning) introduces a feminine counterpart to the river's masculine force, lost in translation.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: hills bowing as the river's authority commanding the landscape
river carrying the yearning of a woman separated from her home

cultural_entities.translation_note: Turel is a named river in Manipur; its cultural specificity as a regional waterway is preserved only as a generic 'river'.
